original_card.question: Can one precisely specified helper-mixing word satisfy a replacement for the inherited H2/K interface?
methods: Derive a replacement interface lemma and price its implementation.
Seek an exact dirty-input or chronological-cut counterexample to the proposed replacement.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A full boundary contract and paid profile; unchanged scalar counts alone are insufficient.

first_step.inspect: Compare the two false H2/K flags with the unchanged paid profile in its README.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write one replacement H2/K implication for a single helper-star operation, then try to falsify it on dirty inputs.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A legitimate replacement could admit a cheaper bit circuit; scalar savings alone do not alter the selected moment.
allowed_variations: Choose one helper-star or quartet instance; narrow to one boundary implication.
scope_change_triggers: Changing only source count or scalar addition count without an interface argument.

actual_scope: Certified bit-side budgets for the proposed priority revision 3 (open #1272, stacked on open #1240): in the coverage-law relaxation of the selected PR589 bit word (fixed local word or most favorable in-window shapes, rank-7 copy carriage, idle mass at the halving-depth cap 45/50/53, fractional counts, no surcharge), each lever and combination at a = 1/99, the joint copy-charge x full-frame-helper surface, and scoped obstructions O1 (copy charge 63, every cap) and O2 (shared centre path vs the full-frame helper floor, halving depth <= 3).
scope_change_reason: The card's helper-interface question is saturated (semantic-D contract #1194/#1311, entrances #1179/#1253, after-B frames #1128) and the register-model card is done in PR #1333 (claim #1317). The proposed revision 3 quantifies its levers on the complex side only; this supplies the bit-side numbers any bit centre-path or helper mechanism must meet at the 1/99 planning target. The bit packing ceiling itself reproduces our merged #1023 and is not claimed as new.
bottleneck_link: A large kappa jump needs both suppliers to advance. This gives the bit side's quantitative targets: which levers reach 1/99 under the coverage law, how many full-frame helpers a given copy charge leaves room for at each admissible halving depth, and that #1272's combined lever relies on rank-16 children beyond the stage window while in-window alternatives (fewer helpers, a second unpaid coordinate) exist. No kappa change.
stop_rule: Stop once every lever, surface boundary and obstruction is certified with exact intervals and the positive controls reproduce the selected bit endpoint and #1240's complex ceiling; report any undecided boundary instead of claiming it.
evidence: RESULT.json: packing ceiling 0.001955918756 (cap 45; reproduces #1023's free concentration); levers x2.771/x1.885/x3.738/x1.642/x2.419; with the shipped local mass, centre free + rank-8 fails (0.00894) while centre free + rank-16 (0.01317) and + two unpaid (0.01076) pass; centre free with ideal data and <= 332 width-8 helpers passes in window (0.01010); two unpaid with ideal in-window shapes passes at full copy charge (0.01179). O1: copy charge 63 fails at caps 42/45/50/53/63 (ceilings 0.006794/0.007944/0.009665 at 45/53/63). O2: shared centre leaves 104/131/145 width-8 helpers at caps 45/50/53 (halving depths 2/3/4; certified k/k+1), below the strict floor 138 only at depth <= 3. Complex: #1240 reproduced; #1272's x6.5 needs rank-16; in window centre free + rank-9 0.00813 fails, two unpaid + rank-9 0.01091 passes. 15 tests pass.

open_questions.question: At which halving depth, under which row-coefficient bound, does a concrete bit construction run?
open_questions.why_it_matters: O2 holds at halving depth <= 3 (caps 45, 50) and flips at depth 4 (cap 53), which the merged elementary-cover row bound admits.
open_questions.first_step: Price the selected profile's row coefficient under the elementary-cover bound at depths 3 and 4 and check the remaining finite guards.

open_questions.question: Can a centre-path-sharing mechanism keep every data register a single rank-7 climb with at most 104-145 full-frame helpers?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The ideal-data rows assume single climbs; shipped shapes leave far less room (e.g. none at cap 45 for copy charge 31.5).
open_questions.first_step: Replay a two-call shared-centre toy on a small E8 sub-word.

open_questions.question: What do the in-window alternatives to rank-16 children cost: a second unpaid coordinate, or fewer helpers (<= 332 with the centre free)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Both reach 1/99 in this relaxation inside today's windows.
open_questions.first_step: Price a second unpaid coordinate in format-limits' (Dfc)/(Win) accounting with its invoice.
